subject: long distance runner
title: What If You Never Stopped Running?

scenes.text: What if you never stopped running? Your legs aren't what gives up first.
In week one, runners crossing America burned energy at a huge multiple of their resting rate.
But the body has a ceiling: about two and a half times your resting burn, roughly four thousand calories a day.
Above it, you can't refuel fast enough. Your body starts eating its own fat stores.
By week twenty, the runners' bodies had quietly cut about six hundred calories a day elsewhere.
So the limit isn't your muscles. It's how fast your body can turn food into fuel.

description:
A 2019 Science Advances study of athletes running the 3,000-mile Race Across the USA, about a marathon a day for months, found humans can sustain only about 2.5 times their resting metabolic rate, roughly 4,000 kcal a day.
After 20 weeks the runners burned about 600 fewer calories a day than their mileage predicted. Researchers think the cap comes from how fast the body can absorb and convert food.

first_comment: The same ceiling showed up in the Tour de France and in pregnancy. What's the longest you've ever run without stopping?
